source: RainPoint app device-information screenshots correlated with retained and live local RF observations

rf.address_mapping_status: unconfirmed because the same field value occurs in reports from other installed HCS026 sensors

conclusions: For both tested product families, the high byte of the 32-bit app device ID equals the catalogued product code.
For the HTV405 association, app address 6 maps directly to 0x86 in paired requests and subsequent idle-link reports.
The HCS026 app-address field is not yet located over RF; a 0x82 candidate in Left Bed traffic is shared by other sensor report layouts.
The Left Bed app address 2 is distinct from its locally observed acknowledgement channel 4, so device address and radio-channel selector must not be modeled as synonyms.
The observed installation order is consistent with the stock gateway allocating monotonically increasing child addresses, but deletion reuse and maximum address behavior remain untested.
The lower 24 bits of either app device ID do not appear directly or byte-reversed in the correlated RF frames and are not promoted as RF identities.
App RSSI is stock-gateway receiver metadata and must remain separate from local receiver RSSI.
The two device-ID examples support a migration hypothesis, not a universal device-ID format claim.
